messages:
tara: Heads up — canary p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~460ms after the optimizer flip. KV miss-rate doubled for the canary slice. No user errors reported yet. deploy-bot queued autorevert (med confidence).

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary p95 breach (p95 > 300ms). Suggested action: autorevert -> v4.0.1 (confidence=0.61). Autorevert scheduled in 90s unless suppressed. Details: possible allocator/eviction regression.

leo: suppress autorevert. We need traces and heapshots to confirm. If we revert now we'll lose span correlation.

ops-ali: running snapshot: `rdwctl capture --scope canary --kinds traces,heap,kv-stats --since 8m --out s3://rdw-dumps/1759801234-canary-snap.tar.gz` — started, ETA ~75s.

cs-kim: tagging CS. No customer impact yet; prepping a short blurb in case we escalate.

tara: pinning canary route and applying manual hold: `releases pin --cohort canary --to v4.0.0 --reason "p95 spike; manual hold for traces"` — done.

eng-docs: note for release notes: record suppression actor and reason.

leo: proposed rollback criteria: 1) If hotpatch unset of `experimental_alloc_v4` reduces p95 < 220ms within 10m -> resume; 2) Immediate rollback to v3.9.8 if error delta > 0.5% or p95 sustained >350ms for 15m. Also log the suppression in the changelog.

deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert suppressed by user hold (actor: leo). To re-enable: `deploybot enable-autorevert --strategy canary`

ops-ali: upload complete: s3://rdw-dumps/1759801234-canary-snap.tar.gz. Quick flamegraph shows increased memcpy and allocation churn in allocator path. Suspect `experimental_alloc_v4`.

leo: request hotpatch unset. Tara please approve so ops can apply and do rolling restart of canary nodes.

tara: approved. Run: `opsctl patch kernelcfg --unset experimental_alloc_v4 --reason "canary perf regression"` then `rolling-restart --group canary --wait 50s`. Ops, you own the restart.

ops-ali: applying hotpatch...

ops-ali: ```patch applied: experimental_alloc_v4 unset
restarting canary-1 ... ok
restarting canary-2 ... ok
restarting canary-3 ... ok
```

deploy-bot: MONITOR: after hotpatch revert, canary p95 dropped from ~460ms -> ~140ms within 4m. Autorevert remains suppressed per operator hold.

cs-kim: posting proactive note: "We paused a small canary rollout for investigation and applied a hotfix; no customer-facing impact observed."

tara: recommendation: unpin and resume a slow rollout: increment 5% every 5m up to 25%, keep autorevert suppressed for 45m to avoid flip-flop. Also create rollback ticket if metrics regress.

leo: preparing rollback ticket runbook in case we need it (ops-RB-1759801234). Postmortem owner: @leo. Draft due EOD with timeline and telemetry used.

eng-docs: I'll update release notes and the #release-log entry reflecting the hotpatch and suppression decision.

ops-ali: resuming rollout: `releases resume --cohort canary --to v4.0.2 --increment 5%/5m --max 25%` — executed.

deploy-bot: INFO: rollout resumed under manual supervision. Autorevert still suppressed.

tara: staying on watch for the next 60m. If p95 > 300ms again, we escalate to full rollback per runbook. Closing thread when postmortem link posted.
